name: Text Spacing
explanation: This criterion requires that no content or functionality is lost when a user overrides text spacing using their own custom CSS (for example, via a browser extension or user stylesheet) up to the following values: line height (line spacing) to at least 1.5 times the font size; spacing after paragraphs to at least 2 times the font size; letter spacing (tracking) to at least 0.12 times the font size; and word spacing to at least 0.16 times the font size. The site doesn't need to provide these controls itself — that's a different, stricter criterion (1.4.8 Visual Presentation, AAA). What 1.4.12 requires is that the page's layout doesn't break when someone else's stylesheet applies this extra spacing: text shouldn't get clipped, overlap other text, or disappear, and no functionality should become unusable. The usual cause of failure is containers with fixed heights or widths combined with `overflow: hidden` (or similarly restrictive sizing) around text — the box doesn't grow to fit the now-taller, now-wider text, so content is cut off.
whoItAffects: People with low vision or dyslexia often rely on browser extensions or user stylesheets (such as Stylus, or built-in reader/accessibility modes) that increase line height, letter spacing, word spacing, and paragraph spacing to make text easier to track and decode — tighter spacing can cause lines to blur together or words to be misread. If a site's layout can't accommodate that extra spacing, these users lose access to content that gets clipped inside a fixed-size box, or encounter buttons and labels that overlap and become impossible to use. This also affects people with certain cognitive disabilities who use increased spacing to reduce visual crowding, and anyone using OS-level or browser-level text-spacing accessibility settings that apply the same kind of override site-wide.
howToTest: Install a user-stylesheet browser extension (such as Stylus) and add a stylesheet that applies to all sites: `* { line-height: 1.5 !important; margin-bottom: 2em !important; letter-spacing: 0.12em !important; word-spacing: 0.16em !important; }` (adjust the em-based values to be relative to each element's own font size). With that stylesheet active, browse through the page's cards, buttons, navigation menus, and body text and look for any text that gets clipped or cut off, overlaps other text or controls, or disappears behind a fixed-size box — that's a failure. Also check that every control (links, buttons, form fields) is still visible and operable, not hidden behind other content that didn't resize.

check.question: A user applies a custom stylesheet that increases line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing, and word spacing per SC 1.4.12. A card component on the site has a fixed height with overflow:hidden, and the bio text inside now gets cut off. What is the correct fix?
choices: Nothing needs to change, since the site itself doesn't have to offer text-spacing controls
Make the card's height flexible (e.g. min-height instead of a fixed height) and remove the overflow:hidden clipping so the text can grow without being cut off
Reduce the font size inside the card so the text takes up less space
Add a 'Read more' link so the clipped text is available elsewhere on the page
